answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance-mandated security patch), and failover (b2) addresses regional degradation, not a primary saturated by heavy settlement writes. b5 is the closest match: offloading report/read queries to replicas previously recovered transactional write latency the same day, which directly targets p99 on the write path without risking customer writes. Circuit breakers (b4) protect against a failing dependency, but no dependency outage is indicated here; verifying b4 confirms it doesn't fit before committing. Add capacity (b3) helped a forecasted peak but is slower to take effect mid-incident; it remains the fallback if replica offloading doesn't bend p99 within the window.
